chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya’qoub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Nu’man, from some of our companions, that he ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Indeed, regarding My servants, you have no control over them»
He said: He has not, over this group in particular, any control
He said: I said: And how, may I be sacrificed for you, while there is in them what is in them?
He said: It is not as you think. His saying: «you have no control over them» only indicates that He makes disbelief desirable to them and faith hated by them.

key_terms.الْعِصَابَةِ: the group, the sect, the community

ai.seo_question: How does Satan have control over believers if the Quran says he has no authority over them?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this interpretation from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), distinguishing between absolute dominion and persuasive influence, thereby resolving the theological tension regarding Satan's power over the faithful. The Imam clarifies that 'control' (sulṭān) specifically refers to the psychological mechanism of making disbelief attractive and faith repulsive, rather than forcing disbelief upon them. This nuanced view underscores the role of free will in the believer's journey, a key concept in Shia kalam.

with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Indeed, regarding My servants, you have no control over them» [15:42].
He said: He has not, over this group in particular, any control.
He said: I said: And how, may I be sacrificed for you, while there is in them what is in them?
He said: It is not as you think. His saying: «you have no control over them» only indicates that He makes disbelief desirable to them and faith hated by them.
